topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: When prioritizing high-revenue services over navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling, link budgets are negatively impacted due to reduced navigation safety margins and increased interference. Advanced algorithms considering real-time link characteristics are crucial to mitigate these trade-offs. Frequency reuse strategies like FFR and adaptive frequency planning can help balance revenue generation with navigation safety margins effectively. Integrating AI/ML with SON and FFR optimizes frequency allocation by analyzing historical data to predict link characteristics, reducing interference and ensuring QoS guarantees. However, this introduces complexity in managing real-time data quality.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of considering link characteristics like latency, jitter, and available capacity when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins. Current solutions often rely on simplified path selection based solely on bandwidth availability, neglecting dynamic changes in link quality.
